content: 1. Avoid using ibrutinib concurrently with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required for short-term use (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 2. Ibuprofen or famotidine can reduce the effectiveness of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 3. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed. 4. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Both imipramine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. UGT1A1 inhibitors also decrease irinotecan metabolism. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. UGT1A1 inhibitors also decrease irinotecan metabolism. 9. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or replace with alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. After discontinuing the strong inhibitor, increase the dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor. 11. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Avoid co-administration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effects of these drugs. 13. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Lansoprazole reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives. 17. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 18. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lenacapavir by mechanisms involving P-gp, UGT1A1, and CYP3A inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Both lofepramine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 23. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both ketoconazole and lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of macimorelin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Both maprotiline and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of ketoconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 30. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged sedation. 33. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 34. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Ketoconazole increases the levels of mizolastine by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Both ketoconazole and moxifloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Nevirapine reduces the levels of ketoconazole by increasing its metabolism. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the nilotinib dose to 300 mg daily for resistant/intolerant Ph+ CML patients or 200 mg daily for newly diagnosed Ph+ CML-CP patients. Allow a washout period before adjusting the dose upward after discontinuing the inhibitor. 40. Both ketoconazole and nilotinib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Nizatidine reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Both nortriptyline and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Both ketoconazole and octreotide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 100 mg twice daily. 46. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg daily. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 47. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of ozanimod by increasing the exposure of its active metabolites. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg daily. 50. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Pantoprazole reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg daily. 53. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per dosage modification guidelines. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 54. Both perphenazine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per dosage modification guidelines.
